import * as React from "react";
import { describe, it, expect, mock, beforeEach } from "bun:test";
import { render, screen, fireEvent, waitFor } from "@testing-library/react";
import { MemoryRouter } from "react-router-dom";
import * as realApi from "@/lib/api";
import { TestQueryProvider } from "@/test/utils";

const txnKeywords: Array<string | undefined> = [];

const call = mock(async (path: string, body?: Record<string, unknown>) => {
  if (path === "GET /api/envelopes") return { income: [], rows: [] };
  if (path === "GET /api/transactions") {
    txnKeywords.push(body?.keyword as string | undefined);
    return { items: [] };
  }
  return {};
});

mock.module("@/lib/api", () => ({ ...realApi, call }));

const { TransactionsPage } = await import("@/pages/TransactionsPage");

describe("TransactionsPage keyword search — debounce + race-guard", () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    txnKeywords.length = 0;
  });

  it("debounces rapid typing so only the final keyword is fetched", async () => {
    render(
      <TestQueryProvider>
        <MemoryRouter initialEntries={["/transactions"]}>
          <TransactionsPage />
        </MemoryRouter>
      </TestQueryProvider>
    );

    // Initial load fires one transactions fetch (this-month, no keyword).
    await waitFor(() => expect(txnKeywords.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(1));

    const input = screen.getByLabelText("Keyword or merchant");
    fireEvent.change(input, { target: { value: "w" } });
    fireEvent.change(input, { target: { value: "wo" } });
    fireEvent.change(input, { target: { value: "woolworths" } });

    // After the debounce window, exactly one keyword-bearing fetch — the last value.
    await waitFor(() => expect(txnKeywords).toContain("woolworths"), { timeout: 2000 });

    // The intermediate keystrokes were debounced away: they never hit the endpoint.
    expect(txnKeywords).not.toContain("w");
    expect(txnKeywords).not.toContain("wo");
  });
});

 * Auth route handlers. Drives the active AuthProvider seam: local PIN sign-in
 * mints a session cookie immediately; cloud email sign-in sends a magic link and
 * the follow-up verify mints the cookie. Neither path leaks which user exists
 * (AuthError is surfaced as a flat 401). The session route reflects the resolved
 * session; signout clears the cookie.
 */

import { Hono } from "hono";
import type { Container } from "../../composition.ts";
import { AuthError, type BeginSignInInput } from "../../platform/auth.ts";
import type { ApiError, ChangePinRequest, ChangePinResponse, SessionResponse, SignInRequest, SignInResponse, VerifyLinkRequest } from "../contract.ts";
import { clearCookie, resolveSession, sessionCookie, UNAUTHENTICATED } from "../http.ts";

export function registerAuth(api: Hono, container: Container): void {
  const secure = container.config.deployMode === "cloud";

  api.post("/auth/signin", async (c) => {
    const body = (await c.req.json().catch(() => ({}))) as Partial<SignInRequest>;

    let input: BeginSignInInput;
    if (body.kind === "pin" && typeof body.pin === "string") {
      input = { kind: "pin", pin: body.pin };
    } else if (body.kind === "email" && typeof body.email === "string") {
      input = { kind: "email", email: body.email };
    } else {
      const err: ApiError = { error: "Bad sign-in request.", code: "bad_request" };
      return c.json(err, 400);
    }

    try {
      const session = await container.auth.beginSignIn(input);
      if (session) {
        // Local PIN: a session was minted immediately. Set the cookie.
        const token = await container.auth.mintToken(session);
        c.header("Set-Cookie", sessionCookie(token, secure));
        const res: SignInResponse = { status: "authenticated", userId: session.userId };
        return c.json(res);
      }
      // Cloud email: link sent, second step (verify) required.
      const res: SignInResponse = { status: "link_sent", userId: null };
      return c.json(res);
    } catch (e) {
      if (e instanceof AuthError) {
        const err: ApiError = { error: "Sign-in failed.", code: "auth_failed" };
        return c.json(err, 401);
      }
      throw e;
    }
  });

  api.post("/auth/verify", async (c) => {
    const body = (await c.req.json().catch(() => ({}))) as Partial<VerifyLinkRequest>;
    if (typeof body.token !== "string") {
      const err: ApiError = { error: "Missing token.", code: "bad_request" };
      return c.json(err, 400);
    }
    try {
      const session = await container.auth.completeSignIn(body.token);
      const token = await container.auth.mintToken(session);
      c.header("Set-Cookie", sessionCookie(token, secure));
      const res: SessionResponse = {
        authenticated: true,
        userId: session.userId,
        idleExpiresAt: session.idleExpiresAt,
      };
      return c.json(res);
    } catch (e) {
      if (e instanceof AuthError) {
        const err: ApiError = { error: "Verification failed.", code: "auth_failed" };
        return c.json(err, 401);
      }
      throw e;
    }
  });

  api.get("/auth/session", async (c) => {
    const session = await resolveSession(c, container);
    const res: SessionResponse = session
      ? { authenticated: true, userId: session.userId, idleExpiresAt: session.idleExpiresAt }
      : { authenticated: false, userId: null, idleExpiresAt: null };
    return c.json(res);
  });

  api.post("/auth/signout", async (c) => {
    const session = await resolveSession(c, container);
    if (session) await container.auth.signOut(session);
    c.header("Set-Cookie", clearCookie());
    return c.json({ ok: true } as const);
  });

  // Change the local PIN. Must be authenticated (the session gates who can change
  // it). The current PIN is re-verified by the AuthProvider with the same scheme
  // sign-in uses; a wrong current PIN or invalid new PIN returns 400 — NEVER 401,
  // which would trip the client idle-lock and sign the user out mid-change.
  api.post("/auth/change-pin", async (c) => {
    const session = await resolveSession(c, container);
    if (!session) return c.json(UNAUTHENTICATED, 401);
    const body = (await c.req.json().catch(() => ({}))) as Partial<ChangePinRequest>;
    if (typeof body.currentPin !== "string" || typeof body.newPin !== "string") {
      const err: ApiError = { error: "currentPin and newPin are required.", code: "bad_request" };
      return c.json(err, 400);
    }
    try {
      await container.auth.changePin(body.currentPin, body.newPin);
      const res: ChangePinResponse = { ok: true };
      return c.json(res);
    } catch (e) {
      if (e instanceof AuthError) {
        // Never leak whether it was the current PIN or the new PIN policy at 401;
        // surface the specific-but-safe message at 400 so the app stays signed in.
        const err: ApiError = { error: e.message, code: "pin_change_failed" };
        return c.json(err, 400);
      }
      throw e;
    }
  });

// ── Envelopes grid (with rollups) ─────────────────────────────────────────────

/** One row in the Dave Ramsey grid, with the four figures and tree position. */
export interface EnvelopeRow {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly parentId: string | null;
  readonly name: string;
  readonly group: string;
  readonly rolloverRule: RolloverRule;
  readonly targetType: TargetType;
  readonly targetAmountCents: number;
  /** Envelope type (ISC-91): income, expense, saving, envelope, or working. */
  readonly type: EnvelopeType;
  /** Active flag (ISC-100). Inactive envelopes are excluded from the budget total. */
  readonly active: boolean;
  /** Archived flag. Archived envelopes are excluded entirely from the grid. */
  readonly archived: boolean;
  /** The period the budget is entered in (ISC-94): weekly, fortnightly, monthly, annual. */
  readonly period: BudgetPeriod;
  /**
   * The date the rollover schedule is anchored on (YYYY-MM-DD), or null when no
   * baseline has been set. Editable per budget; drives the per-transaction running
   * balance schedule and seeds the Edit Budget date input.
   */
  readonly rolloverStart: string | null;
  /** Starting carryover (may be negative). */
  readonly carryoverCents: number;
  /** This-period allocation. */
  readonly allocationCents: number;
  /** carryover + allocation. */
  readonly totalCents: number;
  /** total - spent. */
  readonly leftCents: number;
  /** Depth in the tree, 0 = top level. */
  readonly depth: number;
}

/**
 * A first-class income envelope on the grid (ISC-65, ISC-88, ISC-101). It carries
 * the same four figures as an expense row so the UI can render the two identically:
 *
 *   carryoverCents  starting carryover on the income envelope (signed)
 *   budgetedCents   the budget (the expected/target income) — column 2
 *   receivedCents   actual income that landed in the range, in place of "spent"
 *   leftCents       carryover + received - budget (the running income surplus/deficit)
 *
 * `actualCents` is retained as an alias of `receivedCents`, and `varianceCents`
 * (received - target) is retained for the legacy surplus/deficit view (ISC-99).
 * The old `capitalToExpenseCents` field was removed: the income budget is itself
 * the balancing figure (ISA Changelog 2026-06-27).
 */
export interface IncomeEnvelopeView {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly name: string;
  readonly source: string;
  /** The budget: expected/target income for the range (column 2). */
  readonly budgetedCents: number;
  /** Actual income received in the range; alias of receivedCents (column 3). */
  readonly actualCents: number;
  /** Actual income received in the range, in place of "spent" (ISC-101). */
  readonly receivedCents: number;
  /** Income target for the range (defaults to the budget). */
  readonly targetCents: number;
  /** received - target. Positive = surplus, negative = deficit (ISC-99). */
  readonly varianceCents: number;
  /** Starting carryover on the income envelope, signed (column 1). */
  readonly carryoverCents: number;
  /** carryover + received - budget: the running income surplus/deficit (column 4, ISC-101). */
  readonly leftCents: number;
}

/** A named period selection for the grid (ISC-103). Australian FY = 1 Jul to 30 Jun. */
export type NamedPeriod = "this-month" | "last-month" | "this-fy" | "last-fy";

/**
 * Period selection for GET /api/envelopes (ISC-103, ISC-104). Either a named
 * period (default this-month) OR an explicit from/to custom date range. When
 * both are present, the explicit from/to wins. Omitting everything is this-month.
 */
export interface EnvelopesQuery {
  readonly period?: NamedPeriod;
  /** Inclusive custom-range lower bound (YYYY-MM-DD). */
  readonly from?: string;
  /** Inclusive custom-range upper bound (YYYY-MM-DD). */
  readonly to?: string;
}

export interface GridResponse {
  /** ISO YYYY-MM for the rendered period (the range's final month). */
  readonly period: string;
  /** Inclusive ISO date bounds of the rendered range (ISC-104). */
  readonly from: string;
  readonly to: string;
  readonly rows: readonly EnvelopeRow[];
  /** First-class income envelopes with budgeted/actual/variance (ISC-65, ISC-88). */
  readonly income: readonly IncomeEnvelopeView[];
  /**
   * False when the tenant has zero envelopes: the UI shows the empty "not set up
   * yet" state instead of a misleading zeroed balance (ISC-88).
   */
  readonly isSetUp: boolean;
  /** Total budgeted income across income envelopes (the zero-based denominator). */
  readonly budgetedIncomeCents: number;
  /** Continuous zero-based check: positive = unallocated, negative = over-allocated. */
  readonly unallocatedCents: number;
  /** True when the budget is not zero-based; an alert, never a block (ISC-30). */
  readonly zeroBasedAlert: boolean;
  /**
   * Income capital provided = sum of income budgets over the range (ISC-92). The
   * income budget is itself the balancing figure; there is no capital sub-pool.
   */
  readonly capitalProvidedCents: number;
  /** Total budgeted out: sum of active expense+saving+envelope budgets over the range (ISC-98). */
  readonly budgetedOutCents: number;
  /** capitalProvided - budgetedOut. Zero when the zero-base balances (ISC-98). */
  readonly residualCents: number;
  /**
   * Count of transactions in the rendered period that resolve to NO envelope
   * (unmapped, ISC-20). These sit outside every budget; the UI surfaces them as a
   * single "to be categorised" summary line above the budget sections.
   */
  readonly uncategorisedCount: number;
  /** Signed-cents total of those same uncategorised transactions. */
  readonly uncategorisedTotalCents: number;
  readonly asOf: number;
}

/** The budget-balancing (zero-base) figures, ISC-98 / ISC-99. */
export interface BudgetBalanceResponse {
  /** Sum of income budgets over the range: the income capital provided (ISC-92). */
  readonly capitalProvidedCents: number;
  /** Sum of active expense+saving+envelope budgets over the range: the amount budgeted out. */
  readonly budgetedOutCents: number;
  /** capitalProvided - budgetedOut. Zero when balanced; the residual otherwise. */
  readonly residualCents: number;
}

/** Time-travel view: balances as at end-of-day T (ISC-36). */
export interface AsOfRequest {
  readonly date: string;
}

// ── Envelope detail ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

export interface TransactionView {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly date: string;
  readonly amountCents: number;
  readonly payee: string;
  readonly isPending: boolean;
  readonly isTransfer: boolean;
}

export interface EnvelopeDetailResponse {
  readonly envelope: EnvelopeRow;
  readonly transactions: readonly TransactionView[];
  /**
   * Present only when the resolved envelope is an income envelope (id prefix
   * `inc-`). The four-figure `envelope` row above is synthesised from this view
   * (carryover, budget→allocation, carryover+received→total, left) so the detail
   * UI renders income identically; `income` carries the lossless income figures
   * (budgeted/received/target/variance) for richer rendering (ISC-65, ISC-101).
   */
  readonly income?: IncomeEnvelopeView;
}

// ── Envelope trend: spend-over-time series (GAP-A, ISC-16) ─────────────────────

/** Query for GET /api/envelopes/trend: one envelope, optional inclusive date window. */
export interface TrendQuery {
  readonly id: string;
  /** Inclusive lower date bound (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to the current month start. */

/**
 * Cursor-anchored carryover adjustment. Clicking an envelope's Carryover figure on
 * the budget grid opens this at the pointer; saving posts to /api/envelopes/carryover,
 * which records a traceable carryover.reset event. Responsive: a floating popover on
 * desktop, a bottom sheet on touch. Closes on Escape and outside/backdrop click.
 */
export interface CarryoverAnchor {
  readonly envelopeId: string;
  readonly envelopeName: string;
  readonly currentCents: number;
  readonly x: number;
  readonly y: number;
}

export function CarryoverPopover({
  anchor,
  onClose,
}: {
  anchor: CarryoverAnchor;
  onClose: () => void;
}) {
  const invalidateBudget = useInvalidateBudget();
  const isMobile = useIsMobile();
  const [mode, setMode] = React.useState<"set" | "add" | "subtract">("set");
  const [value, setValue] = React.useState<string>((anchor.currentCents / 100).toFixed(2));
  const [busy, setBusy] = React.useState(false);
  const [error, setError] = React.useState<string | null>(null);

  // Escape + outside-click dismissal and focus trap/restore (m2); the mobile

  const ref = useDismissable<HTMLDivElement>({ onClose, closeOnOutsideClick: !isMobile });
  const pos = useAnchoredPosition(ref, anchor, { enabled: !isMobile });

  // Set replaces the carryover; Add/Subtract apply a delta to the current value.
  // The endpoint always stores the resulting absolute value, so compute it here.
  const targetCents = resolveCarryoverCents(mode, anchor.currentCents, value);
  const switchMode = (m: "set" | "add" | "subtract") => {
    setMode(m);
    setValue(m === "set" ? (anchor.currentCents / 100).toFixed(2) : "");
  };

  const save = async () => {
    setBusy(true);
    setError(null);
    try {
      const res = await call("POST /api/envelopes/carryover", {
        envelopeId: anchor.envelopeId,
        carryoverCents: targetCents,
      });
      if (isApiError(res)) {
        setError(res.error);
        return;
      }
      invalidateBudget();
      onClose();
    } catch (e) {
      setError(e instanceof Error ? e.message : "Could not save.");
    } finally {
      setBusy(false);
    }
  };

  const body = (
    <div className="p-3">
      <div className="flex items-start justify-between gap-2">
        <div className="min-w-0">
          <div className="truncate text-sm font-semibold">{anchor.envelopeName}</div>
          <div className="text-[11px] text-muted-foreground">Adjust carryover (logged as a reset)</div>
        </div>
        <button
          type="button"
          aria-label="Close"
          onClick={onClose}
          className="flex h-8 w-8 items-center justify-center rounded text-muted-foreground hover:bg-accent hover:text-foreground"
        >
          <X className="h-4 w-4" />
        </button>
      </div>
      <div className="mt-2 inline-flex rounded-md border p-0.5 text-xs">
        {(["set", "add", "subtract"] as const).map((m) => (
          <button
            key={m}
            type="button"
            onClick={() => switchMode(m)}
            className={cn(
              "rounded px-2 py-1 capitalize transition-colors",
              mode === m ? "bg-primary text-primary-foreground" : "text-muted-foreground hover:bg-accent",
            )}
          >
            {m}
          </button>
        ))}
      </div>
      <div className="mt-2 flex items-center gap-1.5">
        <span className="text-sm text-muted-foreground tnum">{mode === "subtract" ? "−$" : mode === "add" ? "+$" : "$"}</span>
        <Input
          type="number"
          step="0.01"
          className="h-9 w-28 tnum"
          value={value}
          autoFocus
          onChange={(e) => setValue(e.target.value)}
          onKeyDown={(e) => {
            if (e.key === "Enter") void save();
          }}
        />
        <Button size="sm" onClick={() => void save()} disabled={busy}>
          {busy ? "Saving…" : "Save"}
        </Button>
      </div>
      {mode !== "set" && (
        <div className="mt-1.5 text-xs text-muted-foreground">
          {formatCents(anchor.currentCents)} → <span className="font-medium text-foreground tnum">{formatCents(targetCents)}</span>
        </div>
      )}
      {error && <div className="mt-1 text-xs text-destructive">{error}</div>}
    </div>
  );

  if (isMobile) {
    return createPortal(
      <div className="fixed inset-0 z-50">
        <div className="absolute inset-0 bg-foreground/40" onClick={onClose} aria-hidden="true" />
        <div
          ref={ref}
          role="dialog"
          aria-modal="true"
          aria-label={`Adjust carryover for ${anchor.envelopeName}`}
          className="absolute inset-x-0 bottom-0 rounded-t-2xl border-t bg-popover text-popover-foreground shadow-2xl"
        >
          <div className="flex justify-center pt-2" aria-hidden="true">
            <span className="h-1.5 w-10 rounded-full bg-muted-foreground/30" />
          </div>
          {body}
        </div>
      </div>,
      document.body
    );
  }

  return createPortal(
    <div
      ref={ref}
      role="dialog"
      aria-label={`Adjust carryover for ${anchor.envelopeName}`}
      style={{ position: "fixed", left: pos.left, top: pos.top }}
      className="z-50 w-[min(18rem,calc(100vw-1rem))] rounded-lg border bg-popover text-popover-foreground shadow-lg"
    >
      {body}
    </div>,
    document.body
  );
}

import { ArrowRight, CheckCircle2, AlertTriangle } from "lucide-react";
import type { EnvelopeRow } from "@contract";
import type { ChangeScope } from "@domain";
import { call, isApiError } from "@/lib/api";
import { useInvalidateBudget } from "@/lib/queries";
import { formatCents, cn } from "@/lib/utils";
import {
  Dialog,
  DialogContent,
  DialogHeader,
  DialogTitle,
  DialogDescription,
  DialogFooter,
} from "@/components/ui/dialog";
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button";
import { Input } from "@/components/ui/input";
import { Label } from "@/components/ui/label";
import { Select, SelectTrigger, SelectValue, SelectContent, SelectItem } from "@/components/ui/select";

interface Props {
  open: boolean;
  onOpenChange: (open: boolean) => void;
  rows: readonly EnvelopeRow[];
  /** Optionally preselect the destination (e.g. opened from an envelope row). */
  defaultToId?: string;
}

/**
 * Move-money (reallocation) modal. Names an explicit source (From) and
 * destination (To); the amount leaving the source equals the amount entering
 * the destination (ISC-66). Scope is this-month-only or every-month (ongoing,
 * which edits the recurring template — ISC-67). A live indicator shows whether
 * the plan stays balanced (ISC-69): a same-envelope reallocation always
 * balances; moving from an envelope into deficit is allowed but flagged.
 */
export function MoveMoneyModal({ open, onOpenChange, rows, defaultToId }: Props) {
  const invalidateBudget = useInvalidateBudget();
  // Free rebalancing: any envelope can be a source or destination (ISC-89).
  const spendable = rows;
  const [toId, setToId] = React.useState(defaultToId ?? spendable[0]?.id ?? "");
  const [fromId, setFromId] = React.useState(spendable[1]?.id ?? spendable[0]?.id ?? "");
  const [amount, setAmount] = React.useState("");
  const [scope, setScope] = React.useState<ChangeScope>("this_month");
  const [busy, setBusy] = React.useState(false);
  const [result, setResult] = React.useState<string | null>(null);

  React.useEffect(() => {
    if (open && defaultToId) setToId(defaultToId);
  }, [open, defaultToId]);

  const amountCents = Math.round((parseFloat(amount) || 0) * 100);
  const from = rows.find((r) => r.id === fromId);
  const sourceLeft = from?.leftCents ?? 0;
  // The plan stays balanced when the source can fund the move without going
  // negative. Conservation always holds (out === in); "balanced" here means the
  // source does not fall into deficit.
  const staysBalanced = amountCents > 0 && amountCents <= sourceLeft && fromId !== toId;
  const sameEnvelope = fromId === toId;

  const onSubmit = async () => {
    if (amountCents <= 0 || sameEnvelope) return;
    setBusy(true);
    setResult(null);
    try {
      // Post to the free-reallocation endpoint; the move is recorded as a
      // traceable movement (ISC-90) the History view then surfaces.
      const res = await call("POST /api/move", {
        fromEnvelopeId: fromId,
        toEnvelopeId: toId,
        amountCents,
        scope,
      });
      if (isApiError(res)) {
        setResult(res.error);
        return;
      }
      setAmount("");
      // Invalidate the shared budget queries so the grid and net-position banner
      // refresh atomically (the same money move touches both).
      invalidateBudget();
      onOpenChange(false);
    } catch (e) {
      setResult(e instanceof Error ? e.message : "Could not move money.");
    } finally {
      setBusy(false);
    }
  };

  return (
    <Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={onOpenChange}>
      <DialogContent>
        <DialogHeader>
          <DialogTitle>Move money</DialogTitle>
          <DialogDescription>Reallocate between envelopes. Every dollar is conserved.</DialogDescription>
        </DialogHeader>

        <div className="grid grid-cols-1 gap-4 sm:grid-cols-[1fr_auto_1fr] sm:items-end">
          <div className="space-y-2">
            <Label>From (source)</Label>
            <Select value={fromId} onValueChange={setFromId}>
              <SelectTrigger>
                <SelectValue placeholder="Source envelope" />
              </SelectTrigger>
              <SelectContent>
                {spendable.map((r) => (
                  <SelectItem key={r.id} value={r.id}>
                    {r.name} ({formatCents(r.leftCents)})
                  </SelectItem>
                ))}
              </SelectContent>
            </Select>
          </div>
          <div className="hidden pb-2 sm:block">
            <ArrowRight className="h-5 w-5 text-muted-foreground" />
          </div>
          <div className="space-y-2">
            <Label>To</Label>
            <Select value={toId} onValueChange={setToId}>
              <SelectTrigger>
                <SelectValue placeholder="Destination envelope" />
              </SelectTrigger>
              <SelectContent>
                {spendable.map((r) => (
                  <SelectItem key={r.id} value={r.id}>
                    {r.name} ({formatCents(r.leftCents)})
                  </SelectItem>
                ))}
              </SelectContent>
            </Select>
          </div>
        </div>

        <div className="grid grid-cols-1 gap-4 sm:grid-cols-2">
          <div className="space-y-2">
            <Label htmlFor="amount">Amount (AUD)</Label>
            <Input
              id="amount"
              type="number"
              min="0"
              step="0.01"
              inputMode="decimal"
              placeholder="0.00"
              value={amount}
              onChange={(e) => setAmount(e.target.value)}
            />
          </div>
          <div className="space-y-2">
            <Label>Scope</Label>
            <Select value={scope} onValueChange={(v) => setScope(v as ChangeScope)}>
              <SelectTrigger>
                <SelectValue />
              </SelectTrigger>
              <SelectContent>
                <SelectItem value="this_month">This month only</SelectItem>
                <SelectItem value="ongoing">Every month (ongoing)</SelectItem>
              </SelectContent>
            </Select>
          </div>
        </div>

        {/* Budget-stays-balanced indicator */}
        <div
          className={cn(
            "flex items-center gap-2 rounded-md px-3 py-2 text-sm",
            sameEnvelope
              ? "bg-muted text-muted-foreground"
              : staysBalanced
                ? "bg-success/15 text-success"
                : "bg-warning/15 text-warning"
          )}
        >
          {sameEnvelope ? (
            <>Pick a different source and destination.</>
          ) : staysBalanced ? (
            <>
              <CheckCircle2 className="h-4 w-4" /> Budget stays balanced — {from?.name} keeps{" "}
              {formatCents(sourceLeft - amountCents)}.
            </>
          ) : (
            <>
              <AlertTriangle className="h-4 w-4" /> This move puts {from?.name} into deficit. Allowed, but the
              zero-based alert will fire.
            </>
          )}
        </div>
        {result && <p className="text-sm text-destructive">{result}</p>}

        <DialogFooter>
          <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => onOpenChange(false)}>
            Cancel
          </Button>
          <Button onClick={onSubmit} disabled={busy || amountCents <= 0 || sameEnvelope}>
            {busy ? "Moving…" : "Move money"}
          </Button>
        </DialogFooter>
      </DialogContent>
    </Dialog>
  );
}

content.text:
The plan is locked in three waves:

1. **Wave 1 (running now):** frontend trust fixes + backend server-seam fixes (routes/parity test, zod, timezone, PIN throttling, redaction).
2. **Wave 2 (on Wave 1 completion):** store/domain — `withTransaction` atomicity, allocations de-dup + UNIQUE constraint, Pulse read-model fix + snapshot wiring, backup crypt-gate, 0600 perms.
3. **Wave 3 (on Wave 2 completion):** your budget chronology feature — budget lines get `effectiveFrom`/`effectiveTo`, edit page shows a timeline of previous/active/scheduled budgets, income can change as of 1 August, overlapping budgets sum within a month, and the create flow gets a "Complete the previous budget" checkbox ticked by default (which ends the prior budget the day before the new one starts).

One design rule I've locked unless you say otherwise: budget resolution buckets by **month** — a budget contributes its amount to each month its date range touches, so a clean 1-Aug changeover gives July the old amount and August the new one, while leaving the checkbox unticked makes August the sum of both. Budget edits become append-only versions (that's what makes the chronology auditable) and already-materialised past months are never rewritten.

Waiting on the Wave 1 completion notifications now; each wave launches automatically as the previous lands.

if command -v sqlite3 >/dev/null; then
  echo "=== latest 12 transactions (read-only) ==="
  sqlite3 -readonly "$DB" "SELECT date(posted_at) d, status, amount_cents, substr(payee,1,28), category_id IS NOT NULL AS has_cat FROM transactions WHERE user_id='local' ORDER BY posted_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT 12;" 2>&1
  echo "=== status counts last 7 days ==="
  sqlite3 -readonly "$DB" "SELECT status, count(*) FROM transactions WHERE user_id='local' AND posted_at >= date('now','-7 day') GROUP BY status;" 2>&1
else echo "no sqlite3 CLI"; fi

## FIX 1 — `withTransaction` + atomic money mutations

**Files:** `src/platform/store.ts`, `src/store/sqlite.ts`, `src/store/postgres.ts`, `test/penny-memory-store.ts`, `src/budget/service.ts`, `src/budget/distribute.ts`, `src/server/handlers/envelopes.ts`, `src/ingest/sync.test.ts` (3-line pass-through, see flags)

- `Store.withTransaction<T>(fn)` added with documented semantics: serialised, all-or-nothing, nested calls join the outer transaction.
- **SqliteStore:** hand-rolled `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`/`COMMIT`/`ROLLBACK` (bun:sqlite `db.transaction()` is sync-only). **Design deviation:** re-entrancy guarded with `AsyncLocalStorage` rather than a bare depth counter — a plain counter cannot distinguish a nested call (must join) from a concurrent caller (must wait), and joining a stranger's transaction would let its rollback eat committed-looking writes. Concurrent top-level transactions serialise through a promise queue. `upsertTransactions`/`writeDailySnapshot` were rewritten from `db.transaction()` to `withTransaction` so they nest safely inside the hand-rolled BEGIN.
- **PostgresStore:** dedicated pool client carried on ALS; all ~40 query sites now route through a private `q()` that picks the transaction client inside a transaction and the pool outside — so unrelated concurrent queries are not caught in a stranger's transaction. - **Tests** (`test/store-transactions.test.ts`): "fn throwing mid-sequence leaves NO partial writes visible" (SQLite AND memory), "a nested withTransaction joins the outer…", "a successful fn commits…", "a failure on the second setAllocation leaves the source allocation unchanged", "distribute rolls every leg back when one leg fails". Plus a suite-level rollback test (below).

## FIX 2 — allocations de-dup + UNIQUE + keyed upsert

**Files:** `src/store/schema.ts`, `src/store/sqlite.ts`, `src/store/postgres.ts`, `test/penny-memory-store.ts`, `test/store.suite.ts`, `test/allocations-dedup.test.ts`

- `schema.ts` exports `ALLOCATIONS_DEDUP_FIND_SQL` (log what collapsed), `ALLOCATIONS_DEDUP_SQL` (fold SUM into the lowest-id row, delete the rest — portable correlated-subquery DML), and `ALLOCATIONS_UNIQUE_INDEX_SQL` (`IF NOT EXISTS`, idempotent). Both adapters' `migrate()` run: schema → additive columns → dedup (with per-group `console.log`) → unique index, index deliberately NOT in `SCHEMA_SQL` so a dirty DB can still migrate.
- **Chosen conflict semantics (documented in code + suite):** `putAllocation` upserts `ON CONFLICT (user_id, envelope_id, period)` with **REPLACE** — amount and scope overwritten (a set is a set, never a sum), and the surviving row keeps its **original id** so history references stay stable. Migration-time collapse **SUMs** (preserving total booked money); runtime upsert **replaces**. - **Tests:** suite: "allocation upsert is keyed on (user, envelope, period): one row, replaced not summed", "withTransaction rolls a mid-sequence failure back to a clean state"; `allocations-dedup.test.ts`: "duplicate rows collapse to one with the summed amount" (raw bun:sqlite seeding of a pre-index DB, keeper = lowest id `al-a`, re-migrate idempotent), "after migration a duplicate insert cannot land as a second row", "two racing rolls land as ONE allocation per envelope" (Memory + SQLite, `Promise.all` race).

## FIX 3 — UTC remnants

**Files:** `src/envelope/service.ts`, `src/pulse/source.ts`, `src/server/services.ts`, `src/server/handlers/pulse.ts`, `scripts/pulse.ts`, `test/domain-timezone.test.ts`

- `EnvelopeService` gains an optional third constructor arg `{ timezone?, now? }` (default Melbourne / real clock) — kept off `EngineConfig` so the ~18 existing test call sites needed zero changes; `buildServices` threads `container.config.timezone`. `resetCarryover` and `runningBalances` now use `todayISO(tz, now())`. `src/budget/service.ts` had no UTC derivations (grepped).

- **Tests:** "a fake clock at 2026-07-31T15:00Z stamps 2026-08-01 (Melbourne), not 2026-07-31 (UTC)", UTC-config counter-test, income-envelope variant, "the fake clock … renders period 2026-08 in Melbourne", plus the reworked "currentPeriodKey is YYYY-MM in the budget timezone, not UTC".

## FIX 4 — Pulse read model + snapshots

**Files:** `src/pulse/source.ts`, `scripts/pulse.ts`, `test/pulse.test.ts`

- `StorePulseSource` now types its store as `EnvelopeStore`, loads mappings, and keys spend (and the Holding balance) via the engine's `resolveEnvelopeId` — the effective-dated mapping resolution, falling back to any stamped `envelopeId`, so existing directly-stamped fixtures still work while ingest-shaped rows (`envelopeId: null`) finally produce non-zero spend. Allocation stays the documented target proxy (spend was the broken figure; scope kept tight).
- `scripts/pulse.ts` now builds the `Services` container and calls `EnvelopeService.writeSnapshot(userId, todayISO(tz))` on each daily run. Idempotency = the snapshots upsert `ON CONFLICT (user_id, envelope_id, snap_date)`: a same-day re-run refreshes the row, never duplicates. (The audit `snapshot.write` event is appended per run — an append-only action log, deliberately not deduped.)
- **Tests:** "mapped transactions yield non-zero per-envelope spend", "per-envelope spend matches the engine's activity rollup" (both over MemoryStore vs `computeActivity`), and the runPulseJob e2e extended: "…a re-run does not duplicate the daily snapshot" (double-run → 1 snapshot row per envelope per day).

**Files:** `scripts/backup-db.ts`, `src/server/handlers/backup.ts`, `src/platform/secrets/local.ts`, `test/backup-db.test.ts`, `test/secret-perms.test.ts`

A refusal (or an upload-verify failure) is recorded via `recordBackupFailure` into `backup-status.json` — preserving any prior verified `lastBackupAt`, adding `lastAttemptAt`/`lastError`. - **Tests:** `backup-db.test.ts` (10): plan defaults/override/shape, crypt pass, "a plaintext remote is refused loudly with the fix commands named", unconfigured remote, unreadable config, "the failure shows up as a failed backup with the reason", "a failure preserves the last VERIFIED backup record", "a subsequent verified success clears the failure message"; `secret-perms.test.ts`: "secret.key and secrets.enc are owner-only after a write" (`test.skipIf` off-POSIX).

## Flags — things done differently and why

1. **ALS instead of a bare depth counter** (FIX 1): a flag/counter can't tell nested-join from concurrent-caller; for a ledger, silently joining another request's transaction is a correctness bug. Nested-join semantics are exactly as specified.
2. **Three small out-of-territory touches**, each forced by an in-scope change: `src/ingest/sync.test.ts` (+3 lines — its `FakeStore implements Store` needed the new required port method to typecheck), `src/server/handlers/pulse.ts` (imported the deleted UTC `currentPeriod`; now tz-correct, which is itself a FIX 3 instance), `src/server/handlers/backup.ts` (required so the recorded refusal actually surfaces through the API, per FIX 5's own instruction). `src/server/services.ts` was edited to thread the timezone — the seam the brief pointed at.
3. **Conflict semantics split:** migration collapse SUMs (preserves historical booked totals); runtime upsert REPLACES with original-id retention. Both documented at the SQL and asserted in the suite.
4. **Snapshot idempotency = upsert refresh**, not a skip-if-exists: a later same-day run picks up newly-synced transactions, and "once per day per envelope" is what the row-count test asserts.

Wave 2 is complete and green: 260 tests pass (31 new), typecheck ×3 and lint clean. The store now has real transactions (with an AsyncLocalStorage-based design that correctly distinguishes nested joins from concurrent callers), the allocations table is de-duped with a UNIQUE constraint so the budget-doubling race is structurally dead, the domain layer is fully Melbourne-timezone'd, Pulse now derives spend through the engine's mapping resolution (it was always-zero before) with daily snapshots wired in, and the backup script now refuses non-crypt remotes loudly with the failure surfaced in the app's backup status. Note for later: the nightly backup will now correctly **refuse** to upload until a crypt remote exists — that's the designed behaviour, and creating the crypt remote (it needs a password only you should hold) is on your side of the fence.

3. MONTH-BUCKET RESOLUTION: a line contributes to every month M where month(effective_from) <= M <= month(effective_to ?? infinity). A month's budget for an envelope = SUM of all contributing lines' amounts for that month (each line still respecting its cadence/proration via the existing normalise logic). content.text:
Confirmed — same cause as before, and your example shows it precisely:

- **Jacqui Nolan's $61.00 payment (14 Jul) is still pending at the bank** (`is_pending: 1` in the ledger).
- The category it's under (`15251086`) is correctly mapped to your **Reimbursement** envelope — no mapping problem.
- The **seven similar payments from 13 Jul ($428.00 total) are all posted** and are exactly what your Reimbursement total currently includes.

So the engine is doing precisely what it's specified to do: ISC-23 in the app's own spec — *pending transactions are listed but never counted*. Her payment will move the Reimbursement total automatically the moment your bank posts it, typically the next business day. Nothing is stale and nothing needs re-syncing; the Transactions page shows the row because it lists everything, while budget totals only trust posted money (that's also what keeps your holding-vs-NAB reconciliation honest).

The reason this keeps surprising you is the real defect, and it's already in flight: Wave 3 is adding a pending indicator to the budget grid, so Reimbursement would show its total **plus a muted "· $61.00 pending"** with an explanation on hover — visible in the row's transaction popover too. You'll see at a glance that the money has arrived but isn't bank-confirmed yet, instead of the page silently looking wrong.

If you'd rather pending amounts count straight into the totals (YNAB-style) instead of being flagged, that's a one-rule change — but my recommendation stands to keep posted-only maths and make pending visible, since pending amounts can still change or vanish at the bank.

# Feature A — Effective-dated budget versions (budget chronology)

## Design notes (where I had latitude)

- **Income versioning shape**: income budgets version through the **same `budget_template` lines**, keyed by the income envelope id — mirroring the ISC-19 effective-dated mappings pattern rather than a new table. Income lines never materialise allocations (`ensureMonth` filters them out); the grid/zero-base/trend resolve income budgets live from the lines, falling back to the stored `income_envelopes.budgeted_cents` when an income has no versions. The **first** income version bootstraps the stored budget as an open-ended baseline line, so completePrevious has a real previous version and coexist-and-sum works uniformly afterwards. When a version reaches the current month, the stored row is also updated (it stays the legacy/current-figure fallback); future-dated versions leave it alone.
- **Pure resolution module**: `src/budget/versions.ts` holds all month-bucket logic (`lineActiveInMonth`, `resolveTemplateForMonth`, `resolveAmountForMonth`, `resolveIncomeBudgetForMonth`, `currentLineFor`, `previousDay`, `versionStatus`). No I/O, no clock reads — "now" comes in as a `Period` derived from `src/platform/time.ts` at the handler boundary.
- **move-money / distribute stay in-place**: ongoing rebalances adjust the *current* version (latest `effectiveFrom` contributing to this month) rather than spraying chronology versions — the "trivial same-version correction" allowance. With no contributing line, a fresh open-ended line starts the first of the current month.
- **Pre-materialised future months**: FY grid views roll future months early, which would have made "picked up naturally by August's ensureMonth" silently fail. Version creation therefore re-resolves already-materialised months *strictly after* the current one (bounded 24-month scan); past months are never touched. Future-month allocations can only be ongoing rolls (every edit surface targets the current period), so the overwrite is safe.
- **Request-level schedule**: `effectiveFrom`/`effectiveTo`/`completePrevious` sit on the request (not per line); unchanged lines are skipped server-side, so a bulk wizard save versions only the rows the user actually changed.
- **completePrevious cutoff semantics**: `effective_to = effectiveFrom − 1 day`. A mid-month transition means both versions contribute to that month and SUM — consistent with the locked month-bucket rule.
- **Chronology synthesis**: an unversioned income returns its stored budget as one synthetic open-ended `active` entry (id `<envelopeId>:current`) so the history view is never misleadingly empty.

## Behaviour intentionally changed

1. Ongoing budget edits **append version rows** (fresh ids) instead of overwriting the single template line; unchanged saves still write nothing.
2. Ongoing edits now **propagate to already-materialised future months** (previously they didn't — pre-existing wrinkle fixed by the re-resolve above).
3. `POST /api/envelopes/edit` (income): a pure name edit no longer rewrites budget/target, and an amount equal to the resolved current budget is a no-op skip (previously re-upserted identical values — net effect unchanged).
4. Income budget figures on the grid, zero-base check, and trend are now **month-resolved**; a versioned income's `targetCents` follows its budget. Unversioned incomes behave exactly as before.
5. moveMoney/distribute creating a brand-new template line anchor it at the first of the current month (previously implicitly open-ended from 1970); grid row cadence labels now come from the *current* version.

## Files changed

Engine/store: `src/domain/types.ts`, `src/budget/versions.ts` (new), `src/budget/service.ts`, `src/store/schema.ts` (additive `effective_from`/`effective_to`, idempotent both engines), `src/store/sqlite.ts`, `src/store/postgres.ts`, `test/penny-memory-store.ts`.
Server: `src/server/contract.ts` (`BudgetVersionView/-sQuery/-sResponse`, extended `EditBudgetRequest`/`EditEnvelopeRequest`/`CreateEnvelopeRequest`, `GET /api/envelopes/versions` in `ApiContract` + `API_PATH_SET`), `src/server/validate.ts`, `src/server/handlers/envelopes.ts`, `src/envelope/service.ts` (income resolution, cadence labels, runningBalances/getTrend resolution).
Web: `web/src/lib/queryKeys.ts`, `web/src/lib/queries.ts` (`useEnvelopeVersions`, versions invalidation), `web/src/lib/utils.ts` (`firstOfCurrentMonthIso`, browser-local), `web/src/components/budget/VersionChronology.tsx` (new), `web/src/pages/EditBudgetPage.tsx` (From/To + checked-by-default "Complete the previous budget" with explainer, per-row History affordance for spending **and** income rows), `web/src/components/AddBudgetModal.tsx` (Budget from/until + completePrevious on edit; hidden for income *create*).

## Tests

`test/budget-versions.test.ts` (20): month-bucket activity/overlap-sums/previousDay/versionStatus; completePrevious=true Jul=old/Aug=new; =false Aug=old+new; current-month default reproduces pre-versioning behaviour; unchanged line creates no version; scheduled version inert until its month; open-ended legacy back-compat; past materialised months untouched; pre-materialised future month re-resolved; income old-this-month/new-next-month; baseline bootstrap; stored-row update rules; income versions never materialise allocations; listVersions ordering/statuses/synthesised income/unknown-id-null.
`test/routes-budget-versions.test.ts` (HTTP, via server-test-app): auth/400/404 on versions; scheduled edit chronology + current grid unchanged; income change as of next month over the wire (this-month grid old, next-month grid new, chronology 2 entries); completePrevious=false sums; malformed effectiveFrom → 400.
`test/store.suite.ts` + `test/memory-store.test.ts`: "template lines are effective-dated, append-only versions (budget chronology)" runs against SqliteStore **and** MemoryStore (Postgres compiles the identical SQL; suite-ready).
`web/src/pages/EditBudgetPage.test.tsx` (5): checkbox defaults checked with explainer; default save body (`effectiveFrom` = first of current month, `completePrevious: true`); future From + untick posts through; income schedule via `/api/envelopes/edit`; History affordance renders the chronology with status chips.

# Feature B — Menu force-sync button

`web/src/components/SyncButton.tsx` (new) + wired into `web/src/layout/AppShell.tsx` (desktop sidebar bottom section and the mobile More sheet). POSTs the real `/api/sync`, spinner + disabled while in flight, success invalidates via `useInvalidateAfterSync` (`web/src/lib/queries.ts:136`) and briefly (5 s) shows the synced-transactions count from the response; failure surfaces the endpoint's `message` inline (`role="alert"`) — no fake success. Extracted as a component so it's testable without mocking the session provider.
Tests — `web/src/components/SyncButton.test.tsx` (3): click posts once + count shown; busy state disables re-click (in-flight promise held open, hammering fires no second request); failure shows the honest error.

# Feature C — Pending-activity indicator

`src/envelope/service.ts buildGrid` computes per-row `pendingCents` — signed sum of pending **non-transfer** activity resolved via `resolveEnvelopeId` for the window (asOf-respecting), rolled up over descendants like every other figure. ISC-23 maths untouched. Contract: `EnvelopeRow.pendingCents?` (additive optional). UI: `web/src/components/budget/BudgetSection.tsx` renders a muted `· $23.45 pending` note after Spent (desktop cell + mobile card) with title "Pending at the bank — not yet counted". `TransactionPopover` already flags pending rows with a Clock "Pending" badge — verified, unchanged.
Tests — `test/envelope-pending.test.ts` (3): surfaced + excluded from spent/left, transfer/out-of-period exclusion, parent roll-up, zero default; wire-shape check in `routes-budget-versions.test.ts`; `web/src/components/budget/BudgetSection.test.tsx` (2): indicator shown with title / absent at zero.

# Coordinator addition — create-envelope type regression

`test/routes-budget-versions.test.ts` → "POST /api/envelopes accepts every non-income envelope type (live regression)": `type: "saving"` → 200, type intact on the grid, template line materialised (`allocationCents` 30000); `"envelope"` and `"working"` create cleanly too. `AddBudgetModal`'s catch now explicitly surfaces the server's `ApiCallError` message (call() throws it with the ApiError body text on any non-2xx), so a 400 like the stale-deploy rejection is diagnosable from the UI.

# Remediation Round — 2026-07-07 → 2026-07-14 (v1.4.0)

Executes the before-Basiq bucket of `DISTINGUISHED_ENGINEER_REVIEW_2026-07-02.md`, plus
three owner-requested features. Three waves, each by a dedicated agent against green
gates, orchestrated with file-territory separation. **Final gates: 312 tests pass
(60 files, was 187/37 pre-round), tsc ×3 clean, eslint clean.** Deployed 2026-07-14:
web bundle rebuilt, `penny.service` restarted, migration verified against the live DB
(UNIQUE index present, 0 duplicate allocation groups, effective-date columns live).
Pre-migration snapshot: `~/.penny/pre-deploy-snapshots/penny-pre-v1.4.0.db`.

## Review findings → fixes

| Review finding | Fix | Wave |
|---|---|---|
| Backend Critical — dead routes `/api/move`, `/api/envelopes/edit`, `/api/movements` | Registered/implemented; `API_PATHS satisfies Record<ApiPath, true>` makes contract↔router drift a compile error; parity test sweeps every endpoint | 1 |
| Backend High — no validation, zod unused | `src/server/validate.ts`: zod at all mutation boundaries, integer-cents refinement, strict dates | 1 |
| Backend High — UTC month/day for a Melbourne user | `src/platform/time.ts` + `PENNY_TIMEZONE` (default Australia/Melbourne) threaded server → domain → pulse | 1+2 |
| Security High — unthrottled 4-digit PIN | Persisted `FileAttemptTracker`: 5 failures → exponential backoff (cap 15 min), 429 + Retry-After, covers change-pin, survives restart | 1 |
| Security Medium — log redaction never installed | Installed at both entrypoints via a SecretStore wrapper (lazy-safe) | 1 |
| Frontend High — idle-timer render storm | Deadline in a ref, ≥30 s publish granularity, memoised context; lock semantics proven preserved | 1 |
| Frontend Medium — `call()` returns error bodies as success | `ApiCallError` thrown on every non-OK; error states render honestly | 1 |
| Frontend Medium — key-save claims success on failure; fire-and-forget mutations; modal seeding | All busy/error-guarded with double-submit protection; detail-page seeding fixed | 1 |
| Backend High — non-atomic money mutations | `Store.withTransaction` (SQLite hand-rolled BEGIN IMMEDIATE, Postgres per-txn client, memory snapshot/rollback; ALS nesting) wraps move/distribute/editBudget/ensureMonth/create | 2 |
| Backend High — `ensureMonth` budget-doubling race | De-dup migration (SUM-collapse, keeper = lowest id) then `UNIQUE(user_id, envelope_id, period)`; runtime upsert REPLACEs | 2 |
| Architecture High — Pulse reads always-null `envelopeId`; snapshots never written | Pulse spend via engine `resolveEnvelopeId` (effective-dated mappings); `writeSnapshot` wired into the daily pulse run, idempotent per day | 2 |
| Security High — plaintext backup to non-crypt OneDrive | `backup-db.ts` refuses non-crypt remotes loudly (`PENNY_BACKUP_REMOTE`), refusal recorded in backup status. **Owner action still open: create the rclone crypt remote and purge old plaintext snapshots from OneDrive** | 2 |
| Security Low — world-readable `~/.penny` files | Secret writes 0600, `.penny` dir 0700 | 2 |
| Backend Medium — `saving` type rejected at create | Full type enum accepted end-to-end + HTTP regression test (live-hit by the owner 2026-07-14 on the old build) | 1+3 |
| SystemsThinking/Architecture — Basiq spec gaps | Spec §11: balance re-anchor + parallel-run window (ISC-129..131), provider-prefixed ids + mapping migration (132..134), tombstones (135), bookmark-at-issuance (136) | — |

## Features (owner-requested, 2026-07-14)

- **Budget chronology** — `budget_template` lines are effective-dated (`effective_from`/`effective_to`),
  append-only versions; month-bucket resolution; overlapping versions SUM within a month;
  "Complete the previous budget" checkbox (default on) ends the open version the day
  before the new one starts; income targets version the same way (salary change as of
  1 Aug: July shows old, August new); per-envelope History view with
  completed/active/scheduled chips; `GET /api/envelopes/versions`.
- **Menu force-sync** — sidebar + mobile sheet button on `POST /api/sync`; busy state,
  honest failure, grid invalidation, synced-count flash. Background cadence remains the
  hourly `penny-sync.timer`.
- **Pending indicator** — grid rows show muted "· $X pending" (title-explained) for
  bank-pending activity; ISC-23 maths (pending never counted) unchanged. Resolves the
  "synced but budget looks stale" reports of 2026-07-14 (Jacqui Nolan case: the payment
  was `is_pending=1`; the seven posted payments were already counted).

## Intentional behaviour changes (documented by the implementing agents)

Ongoing budget edits append version rows (previously overwrote in place) and now
propagate to pre-materialised future months; income name edits no longer rewrite
targets; move/distribute anchor brand-new template lines at the first of the current
month; grid cadence labels come from the current version. All 260 pre-round tests still
pass; behaviour changes are covered by the 52 new tests.

## Deferred (unchanged from the review's Bucket C)

Postgres store suite in CI, per-user `EngineConfig`, session/auth hardening
(`PENNY_SESSION_KEY` floor, persisted magic links, full-digest userId, security
headers), per-tenant cron orchestration, master key out of the vault dir, ARIA grid
restructure, query-cache clear on lock, OneDrive plaintext purge (owner action).

content.content:
ISC-69 through ISC-88 are all still `[ ]` in the ISA, yet the task narrative says the work shipped and committed. Either the state file is lying or the verification wasn't actually run per-criterion. Before "done," reconcile each — especially the anti-criteria ISC-71 (pre-existing tests changed must be *documented*) and ISC-84 (version creation must not rewrite historical months). A green 312 does not prove ISC-84; that's an invariant test, not a count.

## Worry 1 — same-day ledger rewrite, live checks I'd demand

Test-green is necessary, not sufficient, because tests run on synthetic data and your migration mutated *real* rows. Two of your changes are data-destructive-capable:

input.description: Prorate mid-month budget versions
input.prompt:
You are a senior engineer making one focused semantics change in BudgetBuddy. Repo: /home/nicholas-wood/Documents/workspace/projects/envelope-os. Bun + TypeScript strict. Baseline gates green: `bun test` = 312 pass / 60 files, `bun run typecheck` (×3), `bun run lint`. Must be green at the end. Do NOT commit or rebuild — the orchestrator deploys.

CHANGE (owner decision, 2026-07-16): budget-version resolution moves from month-bucket SUM to **day-weighted proration**. Owner's spec verbatim: "If they were midmonth I would want them prorated. E.g. the month of 500 for the first half then 600 for the second half would have an aggregated budget of budget/month days * the number of days that budget was effective for. So approx 550."

CURRENT CODE: src/budget/versions.ts — `lineActiveInMonth`, `resolveTemplateForMonth`, `resolveAmountForMonth`, `resolveIncomeBudgetForMonth` currently give a line's FULL amount to every month its [effectiveFrom, effectiveTo??∞] range touches (month-bucket; overlap sums). Read the whole module + its callers (src/budget/service.ts ensureMonth/editBudget/future-month re-resolve, src/envelope/service.ts income resolution) and test/budget-versions.test.ts before changing anything.

NEW RULE:
- A line's contribution to month M = round(monthContribution × activeDays / daysInMonth), where activeDays = number of days in M covered by [effectiveFrom, effectiveTo ?? open], daysInMonth = real calendar length (28/29/30/31 — Feb leap years correct).
- `monthContribution` is whatever the line currently contributes for a full month (mind non-monthly cadences — check how weekly/annual template lines resolve to a month today and scale THAT, do not re-derive cadence maths).
- Full-month coverage → activeDays = daysInMonth → contribution EXACTLY equals today's value (hard regression invariant: all 312 existing tests must pass unmodified EXCEPT any that asserted the old mid-month double-count — the Wave 3 report says completePrevious=false coexist tests use full-month overlaps, which are unaffected; check whether any test asserts a partial-month sum and update ONLY those, documenting each).
- Overlapping OPEN lines that both cover the full month still fully SUM (owner's original overlap rule intact).
- Rounding: Math.round per line contribution, integer cents.
- Applies identically to expense template resolution AND income budget resolution (`resolveIncomeBudgetForMonth`) so a mid-month income change prorates too.
- ensureMonth materialisation, editBudget current-month update, version-creation future-month re-resolve, grid/zero-base/trend income figures all flow through the resolvers — verify each picks the change up (no stale duplicated month-bucket logic elsewhere: rg for lineActiveInMonth callers).

NAMED TEST (the owner's example, exact): July 2026 (31 days), monthly line A $500 effective through 2026-07-14 (14 active days), monthly line B $600 effective from 2026-07-15 (17 active days) → round(50000*14/31) + round(60000*17/31) = 22581 + 32903 = **55484** ($554.84). August = 60000. Also test: February leap year proration; single line starting mid-month with NO previous (new envelope created on the 20th — prorated or full? Owner intent: prorated, it's the same rule; document this consequence in the test name); open-ended legacy line full-month invariance; income mid-month change prorates; completePrevious=false with two full-month lines still sums fully.

UI (small): in web/src/components/AddBudgetModal.tsx and the EditBudgetPage schedule fields, when the chosen From date is not the 1st of a month, show a muted one-line note: "Starts mid-month — [Month] will be prorated by days." (Compute and show the prorated figure only if the data's already at hand; the note alone is acceptable.) One web test that the note appears for a mid-month date and not for the 1st.

Update the design comment block in versions.ts to state the proration rule and the owner decision date. FINAL MESSAGE: what changed, any existing tests you had to update (each justified), test names added, quoted final gate output (counts).

## 1. Getting backups working (about 3 minutes of your time)

The one step only you should do is create the encrypted remote, because it mints the encryption passwords and those belong in your password manager, not in my transcript. Type `! rclone config` in this session (the `!` runs it interactively here) or run it in any terminal, then:

1. `n` (new remote), name: **`penny-crypt`**
2. Type: **`crypt`**
3. `remote`: **`onedrive:Backups/BudgetBuddy-encrypted`** — a fresh subfolder, so encrypted files never mix with the old plaintext ones
4. Filename encryption: accept the defaults (`standard` / encrypt directory names: yes)
5. Password: choose **g** to generate a strong one (1024 bits), same again for the salt when offered
6. **Save both generated passwords in your password manager immediately.** Without them, every backup is permanently unreadable — they are the whole ballgame.
7. `y` to save, `q` to quit

Then just tell me the remote's ready and I'll do the rest: point `penny-backup.service` at it via `PENNY_BACKUP_REMOTE=penny-crypt:`, reload systemd, run a manual backup, and verify it round-trips (upload, listing, and a test restore-read) before trusting the nightly.

## 2. Why "purge" — clarifying, we're not reducing backup coverage

The six files (1.64 GiB) sitting in `onedrive:Backups/BudgetBuddy` right now are your complete ledger **unencrypted** — every transaction, payee, and balance readable by anything with access to that Microsoft account. That was the security review's top exploitable finding. The purge is only those plaintext copies, and only **after** the encrypted pipeline is proven working — at which point they're pure exposure with zero backup value, because the encrypted nightlies plus the local snapshot supersede them. Until then I won't touch them; they're currently your only cloud copies.

## 3. Proration — agreed and being implemented now

Your rule is exactly right and cleaner than both alternatives I offered. Each budget version contributes `monthly rate × (days effective in month ÷ days in month)`. Your example lands at **$554.84** for July (not quite $550, because the $600 stretch covers 17 of 31 days: `500×14/31 + 600×17/31`). Full-month budgets are exactly unchanged, so nothing shifts unless a change is genuinely mid-month; a mid-month income change prorates the same way; and the create/edit forms get a small "starts mid-month — July will be prorated by days" note so the behaviour is visible before you save. The agent implementing it must keep all 312 existing tests green and encode your example verbatim as a test.

I'll deploy it (gates → commit → rebuild → restart) when the agent lands and report back.

════ PAI | NATIVE MODE ═══════════════════════
🗒️ TASK: Step-by-step crypt remote creation instructions

📃 CONTENT:

You're on rclone v1.60, so the prompts below match what you'll see. Do this in your own terminal (the wizard is interactive). Total time ~3 minutes.

**Step 0 — have your password manager open.** Steps 6–7 generate two secrets you must save. If they're lost, every backup is permanently unreadable.

```
rclone config
```

1. At `e) Edit existing remote ... n) New remote ... q) Quit config` → type **`n`**
2. `name>` → type **`penny-crypt`**
3. `Storage>` (the long numbered list) → type **`crypt`**
4. `remote>` — the path it encrypts into → type **`onedrive:Backups/BudgetBuddy-encrypted`**
   (a fresh subfolder, so encrypted files never mix with the old plaintext ones)
5. `filename_encryption>` → press **Enter** (default `standard`)
6. `directory_name_encryption>` → press **Enter** (default `true`)
7. `Password or pass phrase for encryption` — `y) Yes, type in my own / g) Generate random password / n) No`:
   → type **`g`**, then choose **`1024`** bits
   → it prints the password between `>>>` markers — **copy it into your password manager NOW**
   → `y) Yes I have copied it` → type **`y`**
8. `Password or pass phrase for salt` (it will say this is optional but recommended):
   → type **`g`**, **`1024`** bits again
   → **copy this second one into your password manager too**, then **`y`**
9. `Edit advanced config?` → **`n`**
10. It shows the summary — `Keep this "penny-crypt" remote?` → **`y`**
11. Back at the main menu → **`q`** to quit

**Verify it worked** (either you run this or just tell me and I'll take it from here):

```
rclone listremotes          # should now show penny-crypt: alongside onedrive:
```

Two notes. First, save both generated secrets, not just the first — the salt is equally required for decryption. Second, they also live obscured in `~/.config/rclone/rclone.conf`, but that file is on the same disk as the data it protects, which is why the password-manager copy is the one that counts.

Once you've done this, reply here and I'll finish the job: point `penny-backup.service` at `penny-crypt:`, run a manual backup, and prove a restore-read works before we trust the nightly — and only after that do we talk about deleting the old plaintext snapshots.

🗣️ Jarvis: Eleven prompts, two passwords to save; tell me when done and I'll wire it.

content.text:
Confirmed on both counts:

1. **`penny-crypt` has no passwords** — its config holds only `remote` and `type`. What happened during the wizard: the passwords you generated were saved onto the remote that ended up named `crypt` (your first pass through the wizard), and `penny-crypt` got created without the password steps. I removed `crypt` earlier after verifying the encrypted folder had **zero objects** — so no data was lost and nothing is unrecoverable, but it does mean the two passwords you saved in your password manager belong to a remote that no longer exists. **Mark those saved entries obsolete**; you'll generate fresh ones now.

2. The good news from the failed run: the safety machinery worked end-to-end — loud refusal, upload-verify caught `0B` remote, and the app's backup status now records `lastError: "upload verify FAILED"` while preserving your last verified backup (13 Jul). No silent failure, no plaintext fallback.

**The fix — add passwords to `penny-crypt` (~90 seconds):**

```
rclone config
```

1. **`e`** (edit existing remote) → select **`penny-crypt`**
2. `remote` shows `onedrive:Backups/BudgetBuddy-encrypted` → press **Enter** to keep
3. Filename/directory encryption prompts → **Enter** to keep both
4. `Password or pass phrase for encryption` → **`g`**, **1024** bits → **save it in your password manager** (this replaces the obsolete one) → **`y`**
5. `Password or pass phrase for salt` → **`g`**, **1024** → **save this one too** → **`y`**
6. Advanced config → **`n`**, keep remote → **`y`**, then **`q`**

Sanity check before you reply, if you like: `rclone config dump | grep -A2 penny-crypt` should now show `password` and `password2` lines. Tell me when done and I'll rerun the backup unit and do the full verification (upload, encrypted listing, restore-read round-trip).

input.description: Fix wizard parent-budget exclusion
input.prompt:
You are a senior full-stack engineer fixing one reconciliation bug in BudgetBuddy. Repo: /home/nicholas-wood/Documents/workspace/projects/envelope-os. Bun + Hono + TS strict + React 18. Baseline gates green: `bun test` = 320 pass / 60 files, `bun run typecheck` (×3), `bun run lint`. Must be green at the end plus new tests. Do NOT commit/rebuild — orchestrator deploys.

THE BUG (verified against the owner's live data): parent envelopes can carry their OWN budget template line (e.g. env-groceries has child env-supplements AND its own $505.92 line; env-recreation has 16 unbudgeted children AND its own $600 line). The grid's per-row `allocationCents` is ROLLED UP over descendants (see src/envelope/service.ts buildGrid + rollup). web/src/pages/EditBudgetPage.tsx:122 defines `editable = rows.filter(r => !rows.some(c => c.parentId === r.id))` — leaf rows only — so (a) the header total `totalAllocated` (line ~192) misses parents' own budgets: shows Allocated $7,518.68 vs Income $8,624.60 while the server zero-base correctly says balanced at $8,624.60; (b) a parent's own budget cannot be edited in the wizard at all.

THE FIX:
1. src/envelope/service.ts buildGrid: surface `ownAllocationCents` per row — the row's OWN allocation for the period (0 when none), NOT rolled up. Contract: additive optional field on EnvelopeRow in src/server/contract.ts. Confirm how allocations map to rows today (allocMap) — the own figure should be exactly the row's allocation table entry (post-proration, since ensureMonth materialises prorated values).
2. EditBudgetPage: `editable` becomes rows that are leaves OR have a nonzero own budget line (ownAllocationCents > 0 or an own template entry — decide based on what the row data offers; a parent that is pure rollup stays excluded). For a parent row in the editable list, all figures the wizard edits/sums must use the OWN amount, not the rolled amount (check `entryFor`/`monthlyFor` at ~128-140 — they read r.allocationCents; they must read the own figure for parents, and for leaves own == rolled so a single code path using ownAllocationCents with fallback is cleanest).
3. Header totals: `totalAllocated` = sum of own amounts across ALL rows carrying a budget — must equal the server's zero-base allocated figure exactly. With the owner's data: leaves + groceries own 50592 + recreation own 60000 = 862460.
4. Saving an edit for a parent row must route through the same editBudget path targeting THAT envelope id (verify src/server handlers accept it — they key on envelopeId, so they should; test it).
5. Make sure the parent row is visually distinguishable in the wizard (it already renders sections; if parents were previously absent from the list entirely, they now appear — a subtle "includes sub-envelopes" hint near the name is enough if the page idiom supports it cheaply; skip if it would be invasive).

TESTS: engine/HTTP — buildGrid returns ownAllocationCents un-rolled for a parent-with-own-budget + rolled allocationCents unchanged (fixture mirroring groceries/supplements); wizard totals reconcile: sum of own == zero-base allocated (use the server-test-app + a seeded parent-own-budget fixture); editBudget against a parent envelope id updates the parent's own line and leaves the child untouched. Web — EditBudgetPage test: with a parent-own-budget fixture, the header Allocated equals income (balanced) and the parent row renders as editable; regression: pure-rollup parent (no own line) stays excluded.

Update the misleading comment above totalAllocated ("uses every editable line's...") to describe the own-amount rule. FINAL MESSAGE: what changed, files, test names, quoted final gate output, anything interpreted differently.

content.text:
Here's the full picture — good news first: **every manual carryover adjustment you've ever made is recorded**, with before and after values. It's just not visible in the UI yet.

**Your actual adjustment history** (decoded from the ledger's event log):

| When | Envelope | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 29 Jun, 8:39 pm | Adhoc Income | $10,886.05 → $0.00 |
| 29 Jun, 9:42–10:24 pm | Reimbursement | four adjustments bouncing $74.58 ↔ −$74.58 |
| 16 Jul, 6:48 pm | Presents | **−$738.65 → −$60.00** |

**How it works today:**
- **Check:** only via the event log directly (as I just did) — the History page shows budget-template edits only, not carryover resets. That's the gap.
- **Edit:** click the Carryover figure on any budget row (popover with Set / Add / Subtract), or the carryover adjuster on the envelope detail page. Every save writes a `carryover.reset` event with the before/after pair.
- **Undo:** no one-click undo yet, but because the before value is always recorded, undoing is just setting it back — e.g. to undo tonight's Presents change, set its carryover to **−$738.65**. Nothing is ever lost.
- **"Was this manually adjusted?"** — currently invisible on the grid. An adjusted rollover looks identical to a natural one, which fails your app's own "one honest line" principle.

**The fix I'd queue** (small, coherent): surface `carryover.reset` events in the History page (timestamped, per envelope, before → after); put a subtle marker on any Carryover figure that was manually set (tooltip: "Manually set to $X on date — was $Y"); and add a one-click **Undo** in that popover that restores the recorded before value. The data model already supports all three — it's purely surfacing.

One sequencing note: the wizard reconciliation fix (your balanced/$7,518.68 report) is still running and owns some of the same files, so I'll launch this carryover-visibility work right after it lands, then deploy both together and confirm against your real data.

**Bug:** the Edit Budget wizard treated only leaf rows as budget-carrying, but a parent envelope can carry its OWN template line alongside its children (Groceries $505.92 + Supplements child; Recreation $600 + 16 children). Since the grid's per-row `allocationCents` is rolled up over descendants, the wizard's header total undercounted (Allocated $7,518.68 vs Income $8,624.60 while the server zero-base was balanced) and a parent's own line was uneditable.

**Fix:**

1. `/home/nicholas-wood/Documents/workspace/projects/envelope-os/src/server/contract.ts` — added additive optional `ownAllocationCents?: number` to `EnvelopeRow` (the row's own allocation-table entry, post-proration, never rolled; leaf: own == rolled; pure-rollup parent: 0).
2. `/home/nicholas-wood/Documents/workspace/projects/envelope-os/src/envelope/service.ts` — `buildGrid` now sums each envelope's own entries from `inputs[i].allocationByEnv` across the visible months (same `startIdx` window as `aggregateRange`, so it's exactly the materialised/prorated allocation rows and range-consistent); `toRows` takes the map and emits the field. 3. `/home/nicholas-wood/Documents/workspace/projects/envelope-os/web/src/pages/EditBudgetPage.tsx` — module-level `ownAlloc(r) = r.ownAllocationCents ?? r.allocationCents` (single code path; fallback is exact for leaves on older payloads); `editable` = leaves OR parents with `ownAlloc(r) > 0` (pure-rollup parents stay excluded); draft seeding and `entryFor` read the own figure, so `monthlyFor`, section totals, header `totalAllocated`, and the saved `lines` all operate on own amounts; replaced the misleading comment above `totalAllocated` with the own-amount rule. Parent rows get a subtle chip next to the name (same idiom as the existing "inactive" chip) with a title tooltip.

- `test/envelope-service.test.ts` — "own allocation (parent carrying its own budget line)": `ownAllocationCents` un-rolled (50592) while `allocationCents` stays rolled (60592), leaf own == rolled, pure-rollup parent own = 0, and sum-of-own == `budgetedOutCents`.
- `test/budget-parent-own.test.ts` (new file, real Hono app via `server-test-app`) — "ownAllocationCents is the parent's own line; allocationCents stays rolled; own sum == zero-base allocated" (residual 0, balanced to the cent) and "updates the parent's own line and leaves the child untouched" (`POST /api/budget/edit` against the parent id → own 50592→60000, rolled 70000, child 10000 unchanged).

input.prompt:
You are a senior full-stack engineer adding carryover-adjustment visibility to BudgetBuddy. Repo: /home/nicholas-wood/Documents/workspace/projects/envelope-os. Bun + Hono + TS strict + React 18 + TanStack Query + Recharts. Baseline gates green: `bun test` = 325 pass / 61 files, `bun run typecheck` (×3), `bun run lint`. Green at the end + new tests. Do NOT commit/rebuild.

CONTEXT: every manual carryover adjustment already writes an append-only `carryover.reset` event (src/envelope/service.ts resetCarryover → this.event(userId, "carryover.reset", { envelopeId, beforeCents, afterCents, on })) into the events table (cols: user_id, id, ts, actor, correlation_id, kind, payload_json). The owner has 6 real events. NOTHING surfaces them in the UI today. The History page (web/src/pages/HistoryPage.tsx) shows only budget-template history.

PATTERNS TO RESPECT (established this round): new endpoints go in src/server/contract.ts AND its runtime API_PATHS (compile-enforced; test/contract-parity.test.ts sweeps); request/query validation via src/server/validate.ts parseBody or equivalent for GET queries; store changes land identically in src/store/sqlite.ts, src/store/postgres.ts, test/penny-memory-store.ts with shared coverage; web data via lib/queries.ts + queryKeys.ts; timezone from src/platform/time.ts; busy/error mutation patterns per MoveMoneyModal.

BUILD FOUR THINGS:

1. **Carryover history endpoint.** Store port (src/platform/store.ts or the envelope extras port in src/envelope/ports.ts — pick the seam that fits how events are WRITTEN today; find the event-append method's home first) gains a read: list events by kind for a user (optionally filtered by envelopeId in the payload — decide whether to filter in SQL (payload_json LIKE) or in the service; service-level JSON filtering is fine at this scale and portable). New contract endpoint `GET /api/carryover/history` returning entries: { id, ts, envelopeId, envelopeName (resolve; null if envelope gone), beforeCents, afterCents, on, actor }. Newest first. Zod-validate any query params. Register handler; parity test will enforce.

2. **History page section.** web/src/pages/HistoryPage.tsx gains a "Carryover adjustments" section (same visual idiom as the existing budget history list): timestamp (Melbourne-formatted like the rest of the app), envelope name, before → after. Data via a new useCarryoverHistory() hook in lib/queries.ts + key in queryKeys.ts.

3. **Manual-adjustment marker + one-click Undo.**
   a. Grid marker: in the budget grid (web/src/components/budget/BudgetSection.tsx / figures.tsx — find where the Carryover figure renders), envelopes whose CURRENT carryover was manually set show a subtle marker (small icon or dotted underline on the figure) with title tooltip: "Manually set to $X on <date> — was $Y". "Currently manually set" = the most recent carryover.reset event for that envelope is the value now in force (compare afterCents to the row's carryoverCents; if they differ — e.g. a later month rollover recomputed it — show no marker). Derive client-side from useCarryoverHistory(); do not add per-row server fields.
   b. Undo: web/src/components/budget/CarryoverPopover.tsx (and the detail-page CarryoverAdjuster in EnvelopeDetailPage.tsx if it shares the surface — keep it to the popover if the detail page adjuster is a different component) gains an "Undo last adjustment" action visible when a most-recent event exists for that envelope: shows "Restore $Y (value before <date> adjustment)" and POSTs the EXISTING /api/envelopes/carryover with carryoverCents = beforeCents. HARD RULE (anti-criterion): undo only ever posts a beforeCents read from the event log — never computed, never derived. The undo write flows through resetCarryover so it is itself audited. Busy/error state per the popover's existing pattern; invalidate budget + carryover-history queries on success.

13	## Problem

15	BudgetBuddy (envelope-os, v1.3.0, ~21.5k LOC TS) has grown through rapid iteration — envelope engine, zero-based budgeting, PocketSmith ingest, local-first auth/secrets, React SPA — and is about to pivot its ingest layer from PocketSmith to Basiq (CDR bank feeds) and eventually to multi-user. No holistic, cross-domain expert review has assessed the whole system; only a frontend staff review (2026-07-01, remediated in 5 phases) and early product/UX/architect docs exist. Nick needs an evidence-based picture of what is actually built and where it is weak before investing in the Basiq build.
16	
17	## Vision
18	
19	Nick reads four reviews that feel like they came from four different distinguished engineers who each spent a day in the codebase — findings he couldn't have listed himself, each anchored to real file:line evidence, converging on a prioritised improvement plan that de-risks the Basiq migration and the multi-user trajectory.
20	
21	## Out of Scope
22	
23	- Applying fixes or patches to the codebase (review only; the report document is the sole artefact written into the repo).

26	- Reviewing PAI infrastructure or Pulse itself (only BudgetBuddy's coupling to them).
27	- Running the app live or penetration-testing a running instance.
28	
29	## Principles
30	
31	- Findings without evidence are opinions: every claim cites file:line or quoted code.
32	- Severity reflects blast radius on Nick's actual trajectory (Basiq pivot, multi-user), not textbook dogma.
33	- A single-user local-first app is judged as such; "enterprise gap" findings must say why they matter *here*.
34	- Independent lenses first, synthesis second — cross-contamination weakens the review.
